item.title: New Research Tests Whether AI Models Know Their Own Thoughts
item.dc:creator: Ben Brubaker
item.description:
By injecting “thoughts” directly into large language models, researchers are trying to map out AI’s capacity for introspection.

The post New Research Tests Whether AI Models Know Their Own Thoughts first appeared on Quanta Magazine
item.content:encoded:
What’s on your mind right now? You can probably answer this question without thinking too hard about it. Being aware of our own thought processes — a capacity called introspection — seems to come naturally to us. Yet among philosophers and psychologists, introspection is a subject of active debate. item.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Kakaes
item.description:
Unlike other recent AI proofs, this one has been unpacked by human experts. The implications, one mathematician said, are “staggering.”

The post AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now? first appeared on Quanta Magazine
item.content:encoded:
Among the 377 results that OpenAI announced on October 6, 2026, one stood out. It claimed to settle the “quasi-Riemann hypothesis” — a weaker version of the Riemann hypothesis, which is arguably the biggest open question in math. The new proof is, as Jared Duker Lichtman of Stanford University put it, “the most significant AI-for-math achievement so far, by quite a margin.

item.title: He Wants AI Benchmarking To Be a Science, Not a Dark Art
item.dc:creator: John Pavlus
item.description:
Moritz Hardt, author of a new book on benchmarks, believes these “standardized tests” for artificial intelligence are fundamentally broken — but not unfixable.

The post He Wants AI Benchmarking To Be a Science, Not a Dark Art first appeared on Quanta Magazine
item.content:encoded:
Benchmarks are the rulers of AI, in both senses of the word. As measuring sticks, they work according to an extremely simple logic: If you want to know what an AI model can do, devise a standardized test to gauge it. item.title: As AI Closed In on ‘Unique Games’ Proof, Researchers Raced to Beat the Machines
item.dc:creator: Ben Brubaker
item.description:
In the shadow of a rumored AI proof of one of the biggest problems in their field, three computer scientists rushed to publish their own milestone result.

item.content:encoded:
